lesson._phases: As 8 etapas do framework esp-real-world, contrato v1 (public/data/frameworks.json). Somam 55 min: 4+7+6+7+7+10+6+8.

items: Who
Rafael Duarte -- a teacher from Lisbon who joined the school last month. You watched his 8 a.m. class this morning. This is your first feedback session with him.
Why
He asked for it. He knows the class did not go the way he planned, and he wants to hear what you saw.
Outcome
Rafael leaves the room knowing one thing that worked, one thing to change, and how to change it.
Pressure
He will disagree with one thing you say. He is not being difficult -- he was in the room and you were not teaching.
Success
He asks a question back. If he only nods, you were not clear enough to be argued with.

attempt.title: Say one sentence for each. The way you would say it today.
items: What did you see the students doing?
What worked, and how do you know it worked?
What would you change, and what do you want him to do differently on Thursday?

attempt_followup.text: “Sorry -- can I stop you there? When you say it did not work, do you mean the activity, or the way I set it up?”
“They were quiet with me too. Is that a problem, or is that just an 8 a.m. class?”

model.title: What each move asks of him
cards: He pictures the moment. Nothing to argue with yet — and that is why he trusts the rest.
The problem has a place in the lesson, not a person attached to it.
A suggestion he is free to take, leave, or improve.
The turn goes to him. If he only nods, you were not clear enough to be argued with.

model.text: Four moves, in order: what you saw → the part to look at → what to try → hand it back to him.

modelmatch.title: Each phrase is doing a job. Match the phrase to the job.
words: The part I would look at is…
One thing you might try is…
How did that feel from where you were?
defs: Names the problem without naming a person
Adds a second suggestion, smaller than the first
Reports what happened, before any opinion
Gives the turn back and invites disagreement
Offers a change he can accept or refuse

discovery_sort.title: Six lines from a feedback session. Sort each one by what it makes the teacher do next.
cols: He can accept, refuse or offer something else
He can only obey or resist
items: The students were working in pairs when you walked around.
You have to give the instruction before the sheet.
One thing you might try is pens down first.
Half of them heard the second sentence and not the first.
It might help if you check it with one student.
Never explain a task while they are writing.

discovery_analyse.title: Look at group B and group C. Both tell him to change the same thing.
items: Which group leaves him a way to answer you?
Which group would you rather receive, on your first week in a new school?
What is the actual difference in the words -- not in the tone?

discovery_answer.title: Reveal what changes
list: Group B carries might, could, one thing you might try -- the suggestion is on the table, and he can pick it up or not.
Group C carries have to and never -- there is nothing to answer. He obeys or he resists you.
Group A is neither: it is what you saw. It costs nothing to accept, and it is why he trusts the rest.
Same content, three different jobs. You choose the job before you choose the words.
discovery_answer.note: This is the whole lesson. Everything after this is practice.

micro_rephrase.title: Your three sentences from the beginning of class -- said again, so Rafael can answer back.
items: The activity did not work.
What I noticed was…
You have to slow down when you give instructions.
One thing you might try is…
The pair work was the good part.
The students were …-ing when…

Your side
You give the full feedback: what you saw, the part to look at, what to try, and you hand it back to him.
Rafael's side
Friendly, and he was there. He will ask what you mean by one thing, and he will disagree with one thing outright.

wb.label: What worked · One point to build on

retask.title: Say only the part your teacher marked -- once more.
items: Same content. The job of the sentence is what changes.
The change
This time Rafael does not accept the suggestion. He says the instruction was fine and the problem was the group.
What you do
You do not drop it and you do not repeat it louder. Concede what is true, keep the point, and give him something to answer.

tips: keep the observation, drop the verdict
